title: Fresh Food Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The fridge compartment temperature sensor has failed.
fullDescription:
E1 on TCL refrigerators indicates the fresh-food thermistor is out of range. The control cannot regulate cooling accurately.

Replace the thermistor to restore proper temperature control.
videoSearchQuery: TCL refrigerator E1 fresh food sensor

title: Freezer Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer compartment thermistor has failed.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the freezer section thermistor is out of range. Freezer may run constantly or insufficiently.

Replacing the sensor usually resolves the issue.
whenToCallPro: If removal of panel risks damaging evaporator.

faq.a: Yes, to another freezer until fixed.

title: Evaporator Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
E3 indicates the evaporator thermistor has failed. This sensor manages defrost cycles; without it, frost can build up on the coil.

Replace the sensor promptly.
whenToCallPro: If coil is heavily iced, full manual defrost first.

faq.a: Yes if frost buildup is heavy.

title: Defrost Sensor/Heater Fault
shortDescription: Defrost circuit did not operate correctly.
fullDescription:
E4 indicates the defrost heater or bimetal thermostat failed during a defrost cycle. Frost builds up and cooling declines.

Test the heater and thermostat; replace whichever is open.

fixSteps.title: Test components
fixSteps.instruction: Check heater and bimetal for continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in new heater or thermostat.

title: Ambient Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
E5 indicates the ambient thermistor is not reporting correctly. The control uses this to adjust defrost timing and dew-point heaters.

Replacement is usually straightforward.
symptoms: Possibly sweat on door gasket area

fixSteps.title: Access control area
fixSteps.instruction: Open control housing per service guide.

faq.a: Controls anti-sweat heaters and cycle timing.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Display and main control not communicating.
fullDescription:
E6 indicates a loss of communication between the display module and the main control board. Often a loose harness or a failed board.

Reseat cables first; replace if persistent.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Open control area and reseat ribbon/harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Swap display or main board if persistent.

faq.a: Usually yes, but display is unusable.

title: Freezer Fan Fault
shortDescription: Freezer evaporator fan is not running.
fullDescription:
FF indicates no feedback from the freezer fan motor. Cold air distribution stops and both compartments may warm.

Check for ice blocking blade before replacing.

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and allow to thaw for 8-24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If FF persists, replace fan motor.

whenToCallPro: If icing recurs, investigate defrost system.

title: Service Error / Multiple Faults
shortDescription: Multiple sensors faulted or demo mode active.
fullDescription:
SE indicates the refrigerator has detected multiple sensor faults simultaneously or is in service/demo mode. Exit demo mode first; if not in demo, main board diagnosis is needed.

Check display for demo indicator.

fixSteps.title: Exit demo mode
fixSteps.instruction: Hold appropriate button combo for 5 seconds (see manual).

fixSteps.title: Replace main board
fixSteps.instruction: If not demo mode, swap main control.

videoSearchQuery: TCL refrigerator SE service mode exit

faq.a: Sometimes enabled before delivery; exit combo differs by model.

title: Heater (Defrost) Error
shortDescription: Defrost heater circuit open or shorted.
fullDescription:
HE is triggered when the defrost heater fails to draw proper current. Similar to E4 on some models, but more specific to the heater itself.

Replace the heater if burnt out.
whenToCallPro: If work around evaporator is uncomfortable.

faq.a: HE is specifically the heater; E4 is broader defrost fault.

title: Power / Compressor Protection
fullDescription:
PE indicates the compressor's overload/start relay protection has engaged several times in a short period. Causes include low/high voltage, failing start relay, or a failing compressor.

Professional diagnosis recommended.

fixSteps.title: Check voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm 115V at outlet, not on extension cord.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: If relay OK, compressor may be failing.

faq.a: Short term; repeated cycling can damage the compressor.
